research_question: Under a fixed PaySim chronological split and matched SGD training procedure, does access to strictly earlier recipient-history tokens improve fraud-detection ranking compared with current-transaction-only input?

dataset.target: current transaction isFraud; target and historical labels are not input features

split.history_rule: history_step < target_step; tied-step and future events excluded
split.partition_history_rule: training targets use only earlier train-step context; validation and test may use earlier context under the accepted causal contract

A_current_only.input: final current-target token only; exactly the current transaction type and amount channels used by Arm B

B_current_plus_history.input: the same current-target token plus the 17-slot history representation of strictly earlier whole step buckets

arms.controlled_difference: availability of prior-history tokens only; same SGDClassifier family, parameters, target rows, pairwise batch order, training budget, class-weight rule, validation threshold rule, and evaluator

model.shuffle: same deterministic permutation within each streaming batch for the paired arms; classifier random_state equals the run seed

threshold_selection.source: validation only, independently for each seed and arm
threshold_selection.procedure: maximize F1 over sklearn precision_recall_curve thresholds; ties prefer higher precision, then higher threshold
threshold_selection.test_use: frozen validation threshold only; no test selection

outcomes.primary_difference: Arm B minus Arm A, paired by seed and evaluated on identical test rows
outcomes.score_semantics: uncalibrated SGD decision margin; higher means more suspicious; not a probability

uncertainty.unit_of_analysis: seed-level paired metric difference; not transaction rows or independent datasets
uncertainty.summary: mean and sample standard deviation across the three paired seed differences
uncertainty.interval: two-sided 95% Student-t interval for the mean paired difference, df=2
uncertainty.interpretation: descriptive training-seed variability conditional on one fixed test split; no significance claim

evaluation_order: train both arms for all preregistered seeds
select and record validation thresholds for each seed/arm
verify all model and threshold artifacts and freeze them
only then stream the test partition once to score all six saved models
attach evaluation-only test labels after score generation for metrics and row-level exports

row_identity.key: SHA-256 of UTF-8 archive_sha256 + NUL + csv_member + NUL + decimal zero-based source data-row ordinal

expected_workload_estimate.runtime: CPU-bound streaming workload; no reliable wall-time estimate is available from prior manifests

storage_estimate.prediction_exports: approximately 0.1–0.3 GiB total for three compressed row-level exports; estimate only
storage_estimate.models_and_metadata: small compared with predictions; exact size measured after execution

failure_criteria: any causal-history, feature-exclusion, row-count, or label-separation violation
non-finite scores or threshold decisions inconsistent with the frozen rule
a seed/arm fails before the preregistered set is complete
artifact write would overwrite an existing experiment or accepted artifact
limitations: one fixed chronological test split reused across seeds
three seeds provide limited uncertainty information
seed variability does not capture dataset, temporal-window, or domain uncertainty
